rationale: This is an additive recombination of two legs already in the archive rather than a new mechanism, and the two legs work against each other mechanically because VOL of (pi+dp)/lt scales with the magnitude of coverage itself, so NEG(VOL) tilts toward low-coverage, low-profitability firms and partially cancels the trough-coverage leg.

Economically coherent and internally consistent (both legs point negative), but it is a two-component swap on ThinEbitdaCoverageWithDebtBuildup that recycles WorstYearCashCoverage as leg one, and leg two is close to the well-documented net debt issuance/change-in-leverage anomaly, so it reads as an incremental variant rather than a new cross-theme idea.

Peak-relative fundamental drawdown is a genuinely distinct deterioration construct from the level and trend measures already tested, the sign logic is consistent (larger drawdown × higher liability burden → lower returns), though the reviewer should watch for the point mass at zero when the current year is its own 3-year max and for the fact that the un-normalized drawdown is dominated by high-variance, high-level coverage firms.

The claim that the depreciation-intensity leg is "untouched by the archive" is false — CollateralShieldedLiquidityGap used dp/at with the opposite economic sign (capital intensity as pledgeable collateral, i.e., protective) — so the proposal's expected sign is a coin flip against an already-tested contrary story, and dp/cogs is largely an industry capital-intensity sort layered on a standard net-leverage sort.

Cash-flow-to-total-debt is a textbook published distress/solvency ratio and this is also a denominator-and-tax tweak of the archived WorstYearCashCoverage, with the added hazard that near-zero (dlc+dltt) firms produce explosive values that 1% winsorization will not fully tame.

Cash share of current assets is a liquidity-composition dimension genuinely distinct from the che/lct levels already tested, and scaling current liabilities by the operating cost base is a defensible claim-pressure normalization, though the lct/cogs leg is ambiguous since high payables can also reflect available trade credit rather than pressure.
